structured_output.hypothesis: If hard-shelled eggs are never oblate, then essentially no measured egg has its symmetry-axis length shorter than its maximum breadth (length/breadth ratio below 1).
structured_output.pass_criterion: Among all eggs with valid length and maximum-breadth measurements in the dataset, the fraction with length/breadth < 1.00 is ≤ 0.5% (allowing for measurement error), AND no species has a mean length/breadth below 1.00. Eggs with length/breadth below 1.00 also count as oblate only if the shortfall exceeds the estimated measurement error (about 2%).
structured_output.fail_criterion: More than 2% of eggs have length/breadth < 1.00, or at least one species with n ≥ 5 eggs has a mean length/breadth < 0.98. Either result means that oblate eggs are not absent.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'prolate spheroid' is a solid of revolution whose polar axis (egg length) exceeds the equatorial diameter (maximum breadth). 'Oblate' or 'flattened or discoidal' means the polar axis is shorter than the equatorial diameter. Thompson meant a loose geometric description, not a strict spheroid: real eggs are asymmetric (ovoid), so this test uses the axis comparison only, with the ovoid asymmetry ignored. The measurable quantity is the elongation ratio L/B from photographs or images (Preston-style profile fits give length and maximum breadth). Scope: hard-shelled (avian) eggs. The dataset is mostly bird eggs and does not cover reptile eggs. Only length > breadth is tested, not exact spheroid fit. Some owl and kingfisher eggs are near-spherical, so the L/B ≈ 1 boundary is where measurement error matters.

dataset.name: Data from: Accurately quantifying the shape of birds' eggs
dataset.publisher: Dryad (authors: Biggins, Thompson, Birkhead, University of Sheffield)
dataset.why_it_fits: Open download of Analysis.zip (datasets used in the paper's analysis) and programs.zip (Preston.R, Indices.R and test data). The plan uses egg length and maximum breadth, or the elongation index derived from Preston profile fits, per egg or per species, to compute L/B. The Dryad page does not list column names, so the exact fields must be confirmed on download. If length or breadth cannot be derived, the test is undecidable on this dataset, not passed.
